description: The supplied image is not a scientific figure. It is a publisher/archive "Check for updates" icon: a square graphic on a light grey-to-white gradient ground containing a circular emblem built from two thick arc strokes (blue upper-left/right, yellow lower-left/bottom) enclosing a red ribbon or bookmark shape whose bottom edge is notched (swallow-tail). Below the emblem, black sans-serif text on two lines reads "Check for" / "updates". There are no axes, no axis ticks, no units, no legends, no scale bars, no data points, no colour bars, no annotations and no panel letters anywhere. No micrograph, diffraction pattern, spectrum, property curve, elemental map, table, schematic of a process or specimen photograph appears. No material system, composition (e.g. Fe–9Mn–5Al-0.3C wt.%), processing condition (intercritical quenching-annealing) or annealing temperature is printed. Consequently the image carries no microstructural or mechanical information, cannot be linked to the paper's δ-TRIP low-density steel results, and must not be used as pixel evidence for any statement about the steel. Nothing in it can be meaningfully transcribed beyond the icon itself.

observations.observation: The image contains only a graphic emblem plus two lines of text; it is not a data figure, micrograph or photograph of a specimen.
The printed text reads exactly "Check for" on the first line and "updates" on the second line, in black sans-serif type.
The emblem is composed of blue and yellow thick arc segments encircling a red ribbon/bookmark shape with a notched (swallow-tail) lower edge.
No axes, tick labels, units, legends, colour bars, scale bars, panel letters or numerical values are present anywhere in the image.
No sample label, alloy composition or processing condition (for example an annealing temperature or the intercritical quenching-annealing condition) is printed in this image.

The image provides no microstructural or mechanical evidence and therefore cannot confirm any claim in the paper about δ-ferrite, retained austenite, or tensile properties of the Fe–9Mn–5Al-0.3C steel.
